title: Heuristics update: calm/stress specialist pools + cognitive alpha reasoning + code coverage discipline
rationale: Three new generalizable lessons from tonight's scan warrant addition to heuristics.md: (1) regime-dependent specialist pool routing (arXiv:2604.10402) — strategy selection should use a probabilistic stress score not a binary VIX threshold; (2) cognitive alpha reasoning (arXiv:2511.18850) — LLM alpha generation benefits from explicit WHY reasoning before mutation; (3) code coverage as financial math hallucination guard (arXiv:2604.11477) — LLM-generated trading code needs ≥95% coverage before accepting.
content:
### Regime-dependent specialist pool routing
- LESSON: The best strategy/model is regime-dependent, not stable. Maintain a CALM pool (LLM-augmented signal strategies: PEAD, Div Raise) and a STRESS pool (pure statistical strategies: factor-only, no LLM dependency). Route via continuous stress probability = logistic(VIX_z + yield_curve_z + credit_spread_z) rather than a binary VIX threshold. Stress_prob > 0.6 = disable all LLM-dependent layers.
- WHEN: Any multi-strategy portfolio design; RegimeGuard architecture decisions; R35 regime stack.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2604.10402 (Risk-Sensitive Specialist Routing, April 2026). Consistent with arXiv:2604.10996 (LLM features decouple in macro shocks).

### Cognitive alpha reasoning before mutation
- LESSON: Before mutating or crossing over an alpha factor formula, ask the LLM to first explain WHY the current formula is expected to work (economic mechanism). LLMs that reason about mechanism first generate economically plausible variants; those that mutate blindly generate algebraically degenerate or spuriously correlated factors.
- LESSON: Use randomized temperature {0.7–1.2} for generation agents (ensures diversity) and fixed low temperature (0.7–0.8) for quality-checking agents (ensures consistency in validation).
- WHEN: Any LLM-driven alpha mining iteration (R33 QuantaAlpha, AlphaPROBE, or future factor generation rounds).
- SOURCE: arXiv:2511.18850 (CogAlpha, revised April 2026). IC 0.0591 vs AlphaAgent 0.0246 (2.4x improvement).

### Code coverage as financial math hallucination guard
- LESSON: LLM-generated financial math code (factor formulas, backtest logic) must pass ≥95% code coverage test before acceptance. Without this constraint, LLMs generate 'algebraically plausible' but mathematically degenerate code (look-ahead in rolling windows, division-by-zero edge cases, incorrect annualization). Coverage threshold is an 'un-hackable' guard.
- LESSON: When generated code fails validation, run 'Epistemic Autopsy': convert the failure to structured JSON {failure_type, formula, failure_reason, excluded_patterns} and prepend to the next generation prompt as exclusion context. This prevents re-generating the same failure.
- WHEN: R33 QuantaAlpha implementation; any session where Claude generates Python factor code for backtesting. Run pytest with coverage before executing on full dataset.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2604.11477 (OOM-RL, April 2026). Sharpe 0.35 → 2.06 via architectural discipline.
